title: Launch matrix: stakeholder sprint mapping and risk-cushion playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Produce an operational playbook and sprint-aligned matrix that maps stakeholders, owners, and gating signals for cross-surface launches (runtime, console, API). Scope includes: mapping release-train lanes, defining sprint-level deliverables and cutover signals, defining risk cushions (capacity/traffic hedges), and an ownership lattice for rapid escalation. Deliverables: 1) a sprint-by-sprint launch matrix CSV; 2) a gating checklist tied to SLO/burn metrics and dependents; 3) a rollback/rollback-window playbook for staggered rollouts; 4) a stakeholder contact map and on-call rotates for launch week. Acceptance criteria: matrix reviewed and signed off by runtime, console, API leads; runbook validated via tabletop rehearsal; observable gating signals wired to console dashboards and alerting. This ticket coordinates with ENG for capacity forecasts and with Design for customer communication templates.
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Created initial scope after PM sync. Draft matrix skeleton uploaded to Confluence. Asked ENG to provide capacity forecasts for next three sprints.
2026-02-24 Marco Ruiz (ENG): Provided preliminary capacity curves and noted potential GPU headroom shortfall during peak token load. Marked ENG-8721 as dependent (autoscaler tuning).
2026-03-02 Priya Desai (Console PM): Reviewed matrix draft. Requested explicit console dashboard ownership for each gating metric and suggested adding a 'shadow-traffic' verification lane.

2026-03-06 Liam O'Connor: Incorporated shadow-traffic lane. Flagged need for a small pressure test during Sprint 11; assigned to ENG-8789. Set estimate to 5 points based on cross-team coordination time.
2026-03-10 Design review (Maya Chen): Approved customer comm templates; recommended shortening cutover announcement window from 48h to 24h for PLG users to reduce churn.
2026-03-12 Reliability review (Grace Liu): Asked for clearer SLO thresholds for automatic fallback; raised incident-learning link to previous rollout (INC-2025-11) as context.
2026-03-15 Liam O'Connor: Updated playbook with fallback window and rollback criteria. Scheduling tabletop rehearsal for 2026-03-22. Requesting final sign-offs from Eng leads by 2026-03-19.
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Use sprint-aligned lanes rather than feature-buckets to simplify cross-team sequencing (decision by PM sync).
2026-03-06: Add a 'risk cushion' of 20% reserved capacity for first 48h of a major runtime release; decision driven by capacity forecast shortfall.
2026-03-10: Prefer shadow-traffic verification in a canary cohort before full cutover; reduces customer-facing regression risk.
risks: Insufficient reserved GPU headroom during initial ramp could force throttled requests and increase error rates.
Cross-team sign-off delays (console/dashboard ownership) could push the cutover beyond the planned sprint window.
Automated rollback thresholds not tuned correctly may cause premature rollbacks or delayed recovery.
External customer communications may not propagate to PLG users quickly enough, increasing support load.
next_steps: Finalize capacity allocation with ENG by 2026-03-17 (owner: Marco Ruiz).
Wire gating metrics to console dashboards and alert policies (owner: Priya Desai).
Run tabletop rehearsal for cutover and rollback scenarios on 2026-03-22 (owner: Liam O'Connor).
Confirm on-call rotation and escalation roster for launch week (owner: Grace Liu).
Lock final customer communication templates and schedule announcement windows (owner: Maya Chen).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: narrower 24h announcement window reduces churn but increases coordination pressure on external partners; agreed to pilot 24h for PLG cohort only.
Suggested metrics to include in gating: 95th latency, token success rate, autoscaler desired vs actual, error-rate by model, and user-facing throughput.
Related artifact: postmortem INC-2025-11 highlights insufficient KV-cache warming as root cause for increased p95 latency—playbook includes a KV-cache warm-up step during shadow traffic.
Stakeholder owners: runtime lead (Marco Ruiz), console lead (Priya Desai), API lead (Sara Nguyen), SRE (Grace Liu), Design (Maya Chen).
